reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules (the matching tolerance) and getWorstCaseAmount, but adds getExpectedAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it.

duplication.why: Removes four inline missing/number/range dispatches, yet getExpectedAmount re-encodes getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch, leaving two parallel amount resolvers in shared/schedules.ts.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getWorstCaseAmount and is consumed from server, forecast, budget template and client.

scope.why: Only the planning-amount call sites, the new helper and its tests change.

maintainability.why: One function now carries the planning rule, but having both getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount invites confusion over which to use, and schedule-template keeps its own op check around the call.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Call sites route through the new shared helper; getScheduledAmount is left in place for display sites rather than bypassed.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts repeats getScheduledAmount's null -> 0 / number / getWorstCaseAmount dispatch under a new name instead of extending it.

one_place.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts is used by updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, normalizeSchedule, scheduleModel, Balance.tsx and schedule-template (which still pre-selects the ops it routes there).
